headline.headline: BRAVES ANNIHILATE RANGERS, 15-1, TO SEIZE SERIES GRIP
headline.deck: Olson crushes his 26th homer as Atlanta pounds Texas across seven dominant innings
headline.body:
ATLANTA — Matt Olson launched his 26th home run of the season, James Baldwin added his 16th, and Austin Riley his 10th as the Atlanta Braves obliterated the Texas Rangers 15-1 Friday night at Truist Park, taking a 1-0 series lead before a crowd of 40,147 that roared through every inning of a lopsided masterpiece.

The Braves broke the game open methodically. They scored two in the second, four in the fourth, two in the fifth, and four more in the seventh, leaving Texas starter Chris Collyer and the Rangers bullpen battered and shell-shocked. Collyer hit Ozzie Albies with a pitch in the process, adding insult to injury as Atlanta piled on. Winning pitcher Teodo cruised through the Rangers lineup with the lead swelling behind him, and Texas managed its lone run only in the eighth inning when the outcome was long decided.

The Braves entered Friday at 56-40, first in the NL East, and showed exactly why they belong at the top of the National League. The Rangers, sitting at 49-48 and first in the AL West, will need a dramatic turnaround when the series resumes Saturday. Brian Nimmo added a double to join a lineup that peppered the outfield all night, and Atlanta's pitching staff allowed just three baserunners of consequence. The series now shifts with Atlanta firmly in control.

secondary.headline: MUNCY'S 18TH LIFTS DODGERS PAST YANKS IN THE BRONX
secondary.deck: Los Angeles scores twice in the seventh to hand New York its latest home loss
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — Max Muncy drove his 18th home run of the season over the outfield wall in the seventh inning Friday night, lifting the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 2-1 victory over the New York Yankees at a packed Yankee Stadium. The Dodgers, first in the NL West at 62-36, scored both of their runs in that decisive seventh frame after the Yankees had led 1-0 since the fourth.

New York, now 54-43 and second in the AL East, absorbed yet another home defeat in a trend that has frustrated the Bronx faithful all summer. The Yankees had held the slim one-run advantage through six innings before Muncy and the Dodger offense broke through. The announced attendance of 46,450 watched in near silence as Los Angeles walked out of the Bronx with the win in two hours and 48 minutes.

secondary.headline: DRYSDALE DEAL HEADLINE FOR FLYERS AS NHL FREE AGENCY ROLLS
secondary.deck: Philadelphia locks up defenseman Jamie Drysdale on a four-year, $26 million contract
secondary.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The Philadelphia Flyers moved aggressively in the NHL offseason market, agreeing to terms with defenseman Jamie Drysdale on a four-year contract worth $26 million. The deal gives Philadelphia a young, mobile blueliner to anchor their defensive corps as the organization eyes a return to playoff relevance following the conclusion of the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs.

Drysdale, regarded as one of the better young puck-moving defensemen available, gives the Flyers a building block on the back end. The signing comes amid a league-wide spending frenzy as teams use the summer window to reshape their rosters. Fantasy rankings released Friday already place Nathan MacKinnon and Connor McDavid atop the 2026-27 projections, a sign that the hockey calendar is turning even as playoff hockey still occupies center stage.

secondary.headline: NFL SUSPENDS CARDINALS EXEC FOR GAMBLING VIOLATIONS
secondary.deck: Arizona personnel executive Ryan Gold handed indefinite ban as league cracks down hard
secondary.body:
The NFL suspended Arizona Cardinals personnel executive Ryan Gold indefinitely Friday for violating the league's gambling policy, the latest in a string of enforcement actions that signal commissioner Roger Goodell's office has no appetite for leniency on betting-related misconduct. Gold becomes one of the higher-ranking front-office figures to fall under the league's strengthened gambling rules.

The suspension lands during an offseason already busy with roster moves and policy debates. Separately, former Cleveland Browns center Ethan Pocic agreed to a one-year deal with the Baltimore Ravens, and dozens of NFL players continued pushing for permanent grass playing surfaces across the league, a campaign that gained momentum in the wake of the FIFA World Cup held on American soil. The Cardinals did not immediately announce an interim replacement for Gold's role.

column.headline: ATLANTA IS PLAYING LIKE THE BEST TEAM IN BASEBALL, AND THE REST OF THE LEAGUE SHOULD NOTICE
column.body:
Three home runs. Fifteen runs. One run allowed. The Braves did not simply beat the Texas Rangers on Friday night — they disassembled them inning by inning like a team that knows exactly what it is and what it can do. Matt Olson now has 26 home runs before the All-Star break whistle blows. Austin Riley and James Baldwin are hitting the ball as hard as anyone in the sport. This is not a fluke. This is a roster built to win a World Series.

The AL West-leading Rangers came into Truist Park with a winning record and pennant ambitions of their own. They left looking overmatched. If Atlanta keeps this up, the NL East title is a formality and the conversation shifts to whether this Braves team can go all the way in October. Based on Friday night's performance, the burden of proof belongs to everybody else.

story.headline: RED SOX SWEEP RAYS WITH TWIN SHUTDOWNS, DUMP DIVISION LEADERS TWICE
story.deck: Boston blanks Tampa Bay 10-0, then wins 5-3 to seize momentum at Fenway
story.body:
BOSTON — The Boston Red Sox handed the American League East-leading Tampa Bay Rays back-to-back defeats Friday, completing a doubleheader sweep before 36,774 and 34,255 fans respectively at Fenway Park. Masataka Yoshida launched his fourth home run of the season and Omar Narváez hit his third in the opener, a 10-0 dismantling that saw Boston erupt for six runs in the sixth inning alone. Ceddanne Rafaela added a stolen base and a double, and the Rays managed nothing against Boston pitching across nine innings, stranding 10 runners in the process.

The nightcap was tighter but Boston again prevailed, 5-3, riding a three-run first inning that proved decisive. Tampa Bay's Taj Bradley Caminero slugged his 29th home run and Jose Abreu added his 13th, but the Rays could not overcome their early deficit. William Contreras connected for his 21st long ball of the season for Boston, and Rafaela doubled again as the Red Sox bullpen shut the door over the final five innings.

The sweep drops the Rays, who entered play at 56-40 and atop the AL East, to a precarious perch as Boston climbs to .500 at 48-48. Elsewhere Friday, the Atlanta Braves pummeled the Texas Rangers 15-1 at Truist Park, with Matt Olson blasting his 26th home run and Austin Riley his 10th in a seven-run seventh inning that put the game out of reach. The Los Angeles Dodgers edged the New York Yankees 2-1 in the Bronx on Max Muncy's 18th homer, and the Chicago White Sox routed Toronto 12-4 behind four home runs to stretch their road winning streak to three games.

story.headline: WOLVES CLAW PAST CLIPPERS AS PLAYOFF FIELD TAKES SHAPE ACROSS THE LEAGUE
story.deck: Minnesota, Portland, Detroit, Dallas and Chicago all saw postseason action Friday.
story.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves muscled past the Los Angeles Clippers in a bruising Western Conference playoff clash Friday, with Anthony Edwards torching the Clippers defense with his relentless drives to the rim and pulling up from deep whenever the lane closed. Karl-Anthony Towns anchored the paint at both ends, while the Clippers leaned on James Harden to orchestrate their half-court offense, but Minnesota's swarming help defense smothered pick-and-roll coverages all afternoon and proved too much for Los Angeles to overcome.

In the other Western showdown, the Portland Trail Blazers took the Utah Jazz to the wire in Salt Lake City, with Scoot Henderson dazzling the crowd with his first-step quickness and finishing through contact in traffic. Utah's Walker Kessler swatted three shots in the first half and kept Portland honest near the basket, forcing Henderson and his backcourt mates to manufacture points from the perimeter, where the Blazers connected at a torrid rate down the stretch to secure the road victory.

Back in the East, the Dallas Mavericks and New York Knicks delivered the marquee collision of the day, with Luka Doncic and Jalen Brunson trading bucket after bucket in a duel that had Madison Square Garden buzzing on a July afternoon. The Chicago Bulls pushed the Cleveland Cavaliers in a physical contest, and the Detroit Pistons rode Cade Cunningham's playmaking to trouble a Miami Heat squad still searching for postseason consistency, leaving the Eastern bracket wide open heading into the weekend.

story.headline: BLUES LOCK UP MCMICHAEL, FLYERS LAND DRYSDALE AS NHL SUMMER SPENDING SPREE ROLLS ON
story.deck: St. Louis hands McMichael a six-year deal while Philadelphia shores up its blue line.
story.body:
The St. Louis Blues moved swiftly to secure their newest forward Friday, signing Connor McMichael to a six-year contract worth $40.5 million, locking up the recently acquired center through what figures to be the prime years of his career. The deal averages $6.75 million per season and signals a clear commitment from Blues general manager Doug Armstrong to build around McMichael as a cornerstone piece in St. Louis's push back toward Stanley Cup contention. McMichael, who spent his early NHL seasons developing in Washington, now inherits a much larger role with a Blues squad hungry to retool after recent playoff disappointments.

In Philadelphia, the Flyers answered their own organizational need by agreeing to terms with defenseman Jamie Drysdale on a four-year contract worth $26 million, a deal that slots the 23-year-old into the team's top defensive pairings at $6.5 million annually. Drysdale, a former first-round pick whose career was slowed by shoulder injuries in Anaheim, arrives in the City of Brotherly Love with significant upside still untapped. Flyers brass is betting that a change of scenery and increased responsibility will unlock the offensive blueliner the organization expects him to become.

The moves underscore a frantic July across the league, with teams scrambling to fill holes before training camps open in September. Fantasy analysts already have Nathan MacKinnon and Connor McDavid atop their 2026-27 rankings, a reminder that the league's elite remain firmly entrenched even as the middle tier reshuffles. Meanwhile, a quieter controversy simmers in the background after columnist Dan Wetzel argued this week that Carolina Hurricanes owner Tom Dundon diminished the sanctity of the Stanley Cup by placing his entire family on the trophy, a decision drawing sharp criticism from traditionalists who believe the Cup's inscription standards demand far greater restraint.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 SEASON
story.deck: Three franchises swap signal-callers in a frenzied May of big moves and bold gambles.
story.body:
The NFL's offseason reshuffling reached a fever pitch this week as front offices across the league scrambled to secure quarterback depth before training camps open in late July. The Las Vegas Raiders made the loudest splash, agreeing to a three-year, $112 million deal with veteran passer Sam Darnold, betting that a change of scenery and a retooled offensive line can finally unlock the potential that has eluded him throughout his career. The move sent shockwaves through a division already unsettled by the Los Angeles Chargers' ongoing contract standoff with Justin Herbert.

Meanwhile, the Carolina Panthers continued their quiet rebuild by shipping the 11th overall pick in last month's draft to the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for wide receiver George Pickens, a move that signals Carolina's belief in young quarterback Bryce Young heading into his third professional season. Panthers general manager Dan Morgan called Pickens a "proven weapon who can change the dynamic of an offense overnight," while Pittsburgh pivots toward a youth movement under first-year head coach Mike Vrabel, who took over after the Steelers finished 7-10 in the 2025 campaign.

Draft analysts continue to dissect April's selections, with the consensus hardening around the belief that the New England Patriots landed the class's crown jewel by taking Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders fourth overall. Patriots head coach Jerod Mayo has been careful to manage expectations, but minicamp footage circulating among scouts suggests Sanders has adapted quickly to New England's pro-style system. Whether the Patriots can surround him with enough talent remains the central question of their rebuild, one that May's free agency additions have only partially answered.
